intro: You are about to enter the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts, a museum in İstanbul province, founded in 1914. It is housed in the palace of İbrahim Pasha and holds the world's most complete collection of carpets. It was here that the 13th-century Seljuk carpets were first brought together.
history: The museum first opened in 1914, in the soup kitchen of the Süleymaniye complex. In 1983 it moved into the palace of İbrahim Pasha, Süleyman's grand vizier, overlooking the Hippodrome. At its core lies what was gathered from mosques and tombs across the country for safekeeping: carpets, manuscripts and woodwork.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the carpet collection with its Seljuk carpets, the Qur'an manuscripts, the woodwork gallery and the ethnography section.
facts: Did you know? The thirteenth-century Seljuk carpets found in the Alâeddin Mosque at Konya are among the oldest groups of knotted carpets known anywhere — and they are displayed right here in this museum. The building has its own story too: it is the palace of İbrahim Pasha, Süleyman's grand vizier, among the oldest surviving examples of Ottoman domestic palace architecture.
outro: This brings our tour of the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These threads and pages have lasted for centuries; with your care, they will last for many more. Enjoy your visit.
